A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SYNTHIA framework and experimental study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-generation experiments, automatic evaluations, a 36-annotator human evaluation and multiple ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds evaluation with GPT-4o-mini, additional DALL-E scores and generated examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the hierarchical ontology, distance-based sampling, three-stage curriculum, contrastive losses and affordance-only inference. The renamed Section 3.2 and expanded generation description do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ontology-based concept-design task and retain two-, three- and four-affordance evaluations. The additional evaluator and illustrated affordance combinations do not introduce a distinct dataset, domain or task requirement.

E2.justification: v3 adds DALL-E to absolute-score comparisons in Table 2 and Section 4.4; v2 used it as a relative-comparison reference. Stable Diffusion, Kandinsky3 and ConceptLab remain in the corresponding existing comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation using GPT-4o-mini with the existing prompts and criteria. Section 3.1 also changes the reported caption-generation model from GPT-4 to GPT-4o, without establishing that generation was rerun. Existing training sizes, test selection, human-evaluation design and ablation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Evaluation Model Selection analysis tests whether findings persist with GPT-4o-mini as judge. Existing analyses of training size, affordance count, affordance distance, prompt type and curriculum learning are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both report the same agreement procedures and results: 67.5% inter-annotator agreement, 22.3% Cohen’s kappa and 91.25% human–automatic agreement, with unchanged Figure 8 heatmaps. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added.

E6.justification: v3 adds GPT-4o-mini results in Table 2, DALL-E absolute scores in Section 4.4 and qualitative examples in Figure 9. Table 2 reports faithfulness of 4.01 for SYNTHIA versus 4.08 for DALL-E, and a novelty tie of 4.57 with ConceptLab. Numerical results in the matched existing tables and plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The ontology definition, concept and affordance distance equations, and loss equations are unchanged. The Jaccard expression is reformatted equivalently; neither version contains additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same design objective, three principal contributions and reported human-evaluation gains of 25.1% and 14.7%. The rewritten conclusion restates the same scientific contribution.

C2.justification: v3 expands interpretation of relative comparisons against DALL-E, transfer to additional affordances without further fine-tuning, and consistency across evaluators. The limitations remain unchanged. Some new wording overstates Table 2, and Section 4.4 incorrectly attributes a performance drop to training with curriculum learning despite Table 7 showing the opposite.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly reports approximately one GPU-hour of training on an NVIDIA A100. Appendix B.1 expands caption-generation documentation, and Section 4.4 identifies GPT-4o-2024-08-06. Existing hyperparameters, parameter-freezing details and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Zheng et al. on LLM-as-a-judge and Kim et al. on Prometheus. New Appendix D positions the work within NLP and multimodal semantic understanding; the existing related-work discussion is otherwise preserved.

P1.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 and the conclusion are extensively rewritten. The appendices are substantially reorganized: previously separate prompts, human-evaluation instructions and experimental details are consolidated, while supplementary results receive dedicated subsections. Introduction wording, terminology and headings are also edited.

P2.justification: Figures and tables are extensively redistributed and resized, including moving the training-size plot from appendix Figure 6 to main-text Figure 4. v3 adds Table 2 and Figure 9, reformats Figures 1–2 and relocates supplementary displays. Captions are revised, including correcting Figure 7’s reference from DALL-E wins to SYNTHIA wins.

improvement.justification: The additional evaluator comparison, hardware/runtime disclosure and clearer appendix organization provide a limited improvement in evidential support and reproducibility. These gains are partly offset by new reporting errors: Section 4.4 reverses the curriculum-learning comparison in one sentence and overstates superiority despite Table 2’s faithfulness deficit and novelty tie. The underlying results remain available for checking these statements.
